newsitem.title: USA: Court backs Los Angeles airport fee plan -director.
newsitem.headline: Court backs Los Angeles airport fee plan -director.

text.p: An appeals court on Friday upheld Los Angeles International Airport's method of setting the landing fees it charges airlines, airport officials said.

"We feel totally vindicated," said Los Angeles Department of Airports Executive Director John Driscoll. "The Department has been under attack for four years for its fair-market value approach. We are pleased our position has prevailed."

The U.S. Court of Appeals decision, issued in Washington, upheld the department's decision to raise landing fees at the Los Angeles International Airport from 51 cents to $1.56 in 1993 and from $1.56 to $1.97 in 1995, the department said.

In determining landing fees, the Los Angeles Department of Airports asserts that land-use charges are based on their fair-market value, not on an historical value. This method produces $15 million annually in fees for the Los Angeles International Airport, Driscoll said.
"I hope this (court decision) ends the political and legal attack conducted by the airlines," he added.
